instruction.name: ldl.w
instruction.description: load left part of an unaligned 32-bit value and merge it into rd

operands.name: rd
operands.description: value merged with the unaligned part

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 50 --unroll2 200 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 20 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r12, 8; st.d $r12, $r20, 0; st.d $r12, $r20, 64' --asm 'ldl.w $r12, $r20, 0'

latencies.notes: Latency from the destination register, which is also a merge input for an unaligned load, back to itself: a repeated copy closes the chain and reads the load latency directly. L1D hit, 64-byte-aligned buffer.

notes: LBT MIPS-style unaligned load, measured with a 64-byte-aligned stack buffer on LA464.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 50 --unroll2 200 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 20 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22' --asm 'ldl.w $r4, $r20, 4; ldl.w $r5, $r20, 0; ldl.w $r6, $r20, 4; ldl.w $r7, $r20, 0; ldl.w $r8, $r20, 4; ldl.w $r9, $r20, 0; ldl.w $r10, $r20, 4; ldl.w $r11, $r20, 0'
throughput.notes: Eight independent destinations reading the same aligned base, so the body measures the load port rather than a chain.
